title: A single Executive Vote can authorize an open-ended parameter trajectory through the Linear Interpolation Module
content:
A.1.10.3.2.13 defines the Linear Interpolation Module (`lerp`) as "a smart contract tool that allows a governance parameter to be adjusted on a straight-line basis over time, **without requiring additional Executive Votes**."

A.1.10.3.2.13.1 gives the mechanics: each instance is defined by a `start` value, an `end` value, and a `duration`; thereafter "any user can then permissionlessly call `tick` to set the governance parameter to the appropriate value based on the time elapsed." A.1.10.3.2.13.1.2 adds a factory contract (LERP_FAB) that registers active instances, exposes `list`, offers `tall` ("tick all"), and can cancel an instance via `remove`.

The load-bearing part is what this does to governance cost. Normally each parameter change consumes a vote and is subject to the GSM Pause Delay. A `lerp` converts a *sequence* of decisions into a single decision plus a public function anyone can crank — including the delay bypass, which A.1.10.3.2.13 grants explicitly once the instance is authorized.

That is a deliberate amortization of governance overhead onto a pre-committed straight line. The trade is loss of mid-flight discretion: the trajectory is decided once, in advance, and the only interventions available are letting it run or removing the instance.
description: The lerp encodes start, end and duration on-chain; any user may permissionlessly call tick to advance it, and once authorized it acts without the GSM Pause Delay.
